attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, given as his own observation.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'appears to have' hedge, the $100 tier, the timing ('immediately') and the $20 subscribers. It is an evidential hedge on an observable change, not a probability claim, so the factual appearance can be checked.

contract.note: Reading 'rate limits' as the Plus Codex limits changed at launch, counting a cut in any usage window, is a fair and ordinary reading. Testing timing but not causation fits the hedge. The result turns on the per-window reading because weekly totals may not have fallen.

evidence.note: Same-day report: at launch OpenAI 'rebalanced' Plus Codex usage away from longer single-day sessions, which cuts short-window use.
Quotes OpenAI's announcement of the same Plus change, made alongside the $100 launch.
Confirms the launch date and that Plus stayed at $20. Gives no figures for Plus limits.

reviews.rationale: Two reports dated April 9–10, 2026 quote OpenAI saying it rebalanced Plus Codex usage at the $100 launch so Plus no longer supports longer single-day sessions. That is a cut in at least one usage window, made at the launch, which matches the appearance Zitron described. Weekly totals are not shown to have fallen, but the contract does not require that.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words; he cites Karpathy only as a foil.

semantics.note: Keeps the benchmark point, the hyperbolic 'nobody can explain', the 'appear' hedge on the non-coding part, and the recent-months scope.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into parts is reasonable: Part B is left unscored as hyperbole, and Part C is read modestly. Counting expert-verified results on open math problems as extension beyond coding is an ordinary reading, since the passage itself discusses math.

evidence.note: METR (Mar 2026): the automated grader scores about 24pp above maintainer merges, and real-world scores are roughly half. Supports Part A, though the newest model tested is Sonnet 4.5.
Rényi Institute (Jan 2026), citing Tao's database: GPT-5.2 fully solved open Erdős problems. A verified result outside coding inside the period, which cuts against Part C.

reviews.rationale: Part A holds: METR found SWE-bench passes far exceed what maintainers would merge. Part C fails under the contract: in January 2026, recent models solved open Erdős problems, recorded in Tao's database, a verified result outside coding before the post. Tao's 'low-hanging fruit' caveat weakens this but does not remove it. Part B is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the causal premise (no knowledge or thought; interpretation from training data), the firm 'will make mistakes', and the 'might' on the multi-agent consequence.

contract.note: Leaving it unscored is fair. The premises about knowledge and thought have no agreed test, the conclusion that LLMs make mistakes is uncontroversial and does not test the cause, and the multi-agent consequence is hedged with 'might'.

evidence.note: Shows multi-agent LLM failures are documented and common. Cannot test whether LLMs lack knowledge or thought.

reviews.rationale: The claim rests on philosophical premises with no operational test. Its testable conclusion (LLMs make mistakes) is not in dispute and does not separate his causal account from others. The downstream failure is phrased as 'might', so it is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, addressed to OpenAI and Anthropic subscribers.

semantics.note: A firm statement about the present state. 'No way to fix' adds an impossibility element that edges toward prediction, but treating the whole as an observation is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading 'sustainable' as subscription cost to serve versus price is an ordinary reading. 'Sustainable' could also mean company-wide profitability, and the choice could change the result. The contract flags this.

evidence.note: Anthropic's company-wide 2025 gross margin was positive, but about 86% of revenue was API. Different metric; it does not isolate subscriptions.
Large company-wide EBITDA/EBIT losses. These include training and all product lines, not the cost of serving subscriptions.
August 2026 change to Plus limits, outside the target period. Says nothing about whether the price covers the cost.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs subscription-level unit economics. The packet has only company-wide gross margins (positive) and net losses (large), which point in opposite directions and do not isolate subscriptions. Nothing settles 'no way to fix' either. The evidence does not resolve the claim.
